28:2: These are the verses of the clear Book.
28:3: We recite to you from the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth for a people who believe.
28:4: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and divided its people into factions, weakening a group among them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive; indeed, he was of the corrupters.
28:5: And We desire to bestow favor upon those who were weakened in the land, to make them leaders and to make them the inheritors,
28:6: And to establish them in the land and to show Pharaoh, Haman, and their armies that which they feared from them.
28:7: We revealed to the mother of Moses: 'Suckle him; whenever you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve; indeed, We will return him to you and make him of the messengers.'
28:8: The family of Pharaoh picked him up so that he might become an enemy and grief to them. Indeed, Pharaoh, Haman, and their armies were sinners.
28:9: Pharaoh's wife said: 'This is a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; it may be that he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a child.' And they were not aware.
28:10: The heart of Moses' mother became empty; she was almost about to disclose him, had We not strengthened her heart so that she would be of the believers.
28:11: She said to his sister: 'Follow him.' So she watched him from afar, and they were not aware.
28:12: We had previously forbidden wet-nurses to him. His sister said: 'Shall I point out to you a household that will look after him for you and give him good counsel?'
28:13: Thus We returned him to his mother so that her eye might be comforted, that she might not grieve, and that she might know that the promise of Allah is true; but most of them do not know.
28:14: And when he reached his age of full maturity and became firmly established, We gave him judgment and knowledge; and thus do We reward the good-doers.
28:15: He entered the city at a time of heedlessness of its people. He found two men fighting there: one was from his partisans, and the other was from his enemies. The one who was from his partisans asked him for help against the one from his enemies. Moses struck him with a fist and finished him off. Moses said: 'This is of the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy.'
28:16: He said, 'My Rabb, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me.' For this reason, He forgave him; indeed, He Himself is the Oft-Forgiving, the Merciful.
28:17: He said: 'My Rabb, by the favor You have bestowed upon me, I will never again be a helper to the criminals.'
28:18: Thus he entered the morning in the city, fearful and watchful. Suddenly, the one who had asked for his help yesterday was crying out for help. Moses said to him: 'Indeed, you are clearly an unruly one.'
28:19: When he wanted to seize the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said: 'O Moses, do you want to kill me just as you killed a soul yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not want to be among the reformers.'
28:20: A man came running from the farthest part of the city. He said: 'O Moses, the chiefs are conferring about you to kill you, so leave at once. Indeed, I am of those who give sincere advice to you.'
28:21: So he left from there, fearful and watchful. He said: 'My Rabb, save me from the wrongdoing people.'
28:22: When he turned towards Midian, he said: 'It may be that my Rabb will guide me to the right of the way.'
28:23: When he arrived at the water of Midian, he found there a group of people drawing water. And behind them he found two women keeping their animals away from the water. He said: 'What is your concern?' They said: 'We cannot water until the shepherds water their animals and leave. And our father is a very old man.'
28:24: So he watered for them. Then he withdrew to the shade and said: 'My Rabb, indeed I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.'
28:25: Then one of the two women came to him, walking bashfully. She said: 'My father is calling you so that he may reward you for having watered for us.' When Moses came to him and recounted the story, he said: 'Do not fear; you have been saved from the wrongdoing people.'
28:26: One of the two women said: 'O my dear father, hire him. Indeed, the best of those you hire is the strong and trustworthy one.'
28:27: He said: 'Indeed, I wish to marry one of these two daughters of mine to you on the condition that you work for me for eight years. But if you complete ten years, that will be from you. I do not wish to cause difficulty for you. If Allah wills, you will find me among the righteous.'
28:28: He said: 'That is between me and you. Whichever term I complete, there is no enmity against me. And Allah is Trustee over what we say.'
28:29: When Moses had completed the term and set out with his family, he noticed a fire from the side of Mount Tur. He said to his family: 'Wait, I have noticed a fire. Perhaps I may bring you some news from it, or bring a burning ember so that you may warm yourselves.'
28:30: When he came to it, he was called from the right bank of the valley, from the tree in the blessed place: 'O Moses, indeed I am Allah, the Rabb of the worlds.'
28:31: 'And cast down your staff.' When he saw it moving, as if it were a snake, he turned his back and fled, and did not turn back. 'O Moses! Come back, do not fear; indeed, you are among those who are secure.'
28:32: 'Put your hand into your bosom, it will come out white without blemish, and draw your wing to yourself against fear. So these two are two proofs from your Rabb to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they are a defiantly disobedient people.'
28:33: He says: 'My Rabb, indeed I killed a soul from among them, so I fear that they will kill me.'
28:34: 'And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in speech than I. Send him with me as a helper that he may confirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.'
28:35: He says: 'We will strengthen your arm with your brother and give you both authority, so they will not reach you. With Our signs, both of you and those who follow you will be the victors.'
28:36: When Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said: 'This is nothing but an invented magic, and we have not heard of this among our ancient forefathers.'
28:37: Moses said: 'My Rabb knows best who comes with guidance from His presence and for whom the ultimate end of the home will be. Indeed, the wrongdoers do not succeed.'
28:38: Pharaoh said: 'O chiefs, I have not known for you any god other than me. Fire up for me, O Haman, upon the clay, and build a high tower for me so that I may look at the God of Moses. And indeed, I think he is of the liars.'
28:39: He and his soldiers grew arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.
28:40: Thereupon We seized him and his armies and threw them into the sea. So look at how the end of the wrongdoers was.
28:41: And We made them leaders calling to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.
28:42: And in this world We made a curse follow them, and on the Day of Resurrection they are among the ugly.
28:43: And by oath, after We destroyed the first generations, We gave Moses the Book; as insights for people, a guidance and mercy, so that they might take heed.
28:44: And you were not on the western side when We decreed the command to Moses, and you were not among the witnesses.
28:45: But We created generations, and lifespans were prolonged over them. And you were not a dweller among the people of Madyan, reciting Our signs to them. But We were the senders of messengers.
28:46: And you were not beside the Mount (Tur) when We called out. But as a mercy from your Rabb, so that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, you were sent.
28:47: And were it not that an affliction would strike them because of what their hands had sent ahead, they would have said: 'Our Rabb, if only You had sent us a messenger so that we might follow Your signs and be among the believers.'
28:48: But when the truth came to them from Our presence, they said: 'If only he were given the like of what was given to Moses.' Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said: '(These are) two magics supporting each other'; and they said: 'We are disbelievers in all of them.'
28:49: Say: 'If you are truthful, bring a book from Allah that guides better than those two, so that I may follow it.'
28:50: If they cannot answer you, know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his own desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
28:51: And by oath, We conveyed the word to them consecutively, so that perhaps they might take heed.
28:52: Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it.
28:53: When it is recited to them, they say: 'We have believed in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Rabb. Indeed, even before it, we were Muslims.'
28:54: Those will be given their reward twice because they were patient, and they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them.
28:55: And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say: 'Our deeds are for us, and your deeds are for you. Peace be upon you.'
28:56: Indeed, you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He knows best those who are guided.
28:57: And they said: 'If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land.' Did We not establish them in a secure Sanctuary (Harem) to which the fruits of all things are gathered as a provision from Our presence? But most of them do not know.
28:58: And how many a city We destroyed that had become insolent in its livelihood. So these are their dwellings, which were not inhabited after them except for a very little (while). And We are the inheritors.
28:59: And your Rabb is not a destroyer of cities until He sends to their mother a messenger reciting Our signs to them. And We are not destroyers of cities unless their people are wrongdoers.
28:60: Whatever thing you have been given is an enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment, while what is with Allah is better and more lasting.
28:61: Then, is one to whom We have promised a good promise and who will meet it like one to whom We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection will be among those brought forth?
28:62: And on that day He will call out to them and say: 'Where are My partners whom you used to claim?'
28:63: Those upon whom the word has come true will say: 'Our Rabb, these are the ones whom we led astray; we led them astray just as we ourselves went astray. We take refuge in You; they were not worshipping us.'
28:64: And it will be said: 'Call your partners.' So they will call them, but they will not answer them. And they will see the punishment. If only they had been rightly guided.
28:65: That day He will call out to them and say: 'What answer did you give to the messengers?'
28:66: That day the news will be blinded to them, so they cannot ask one another.
28:67: Whoever repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, it is hoped that he will be among the successful.
28:68: Your Rabb creates what He wills and chooses; for them there is no choice. Allah is exalted and high above what they associate (with Him).
28:69: Your Rabb knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
28:70: He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. Praise is His in the first and the last, and judgment is His, and to Him you will be returned.
28:71: Say: 'Have you seen: if Allah made the night continuous over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is there other than Allah to bring you light? Do you not hear?'
28:72: Say: 'Have you seen: if Allah made the day continuous over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is there other than Allah to bring you a night in which you rest? Do you not see?'
28:73: Because of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, so that you might rest therein and seek from His bounty, and perhaps you will give thanks.
28:74: That day He will call out to them and say: 'Where are My partners whom you used to claim?'
28:75: And We drew out a witness from every nation and said: 'Bring your proof.' Thus they knew that the truth belongs to Allah, and what they used to fabricate vanished from them.
28:76: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, and he transgressed against them. And We had given him such treasures that their keys were heavy for a band of strong men. His people had said to him: 'Do not rejoice; indeed, Allah does not love the exultant.'
28:77: Seek the home of the Hereafter with what Allah has given you, and do not forget your share of the world, and do good as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the earth; indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters.
28:78: He said: 'This was given to me only because of a knowledge with me.' Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him many generations who were stronger than him in power and greater in accumulation?
28:79: Then he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desire the worldly life said: 'If only we had the like of what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is the owner of a great share.'
28:80: And those who were given knowledge said: 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for whoever believes and does righteous deeds.'
28:81: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home; he had no company to help him against Allah, and he was not among the helped.
28:82: And those who wished to be in his place yesterday began to say: 'Ah! So it is that Allah extends provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it. If Allah had not favored us, He would have made us sink as well. Ah! So it is that the disbelievers will never succeed.'
28:83: That home of the Hereafter We make for those who do not desire haughtiness in the earth nor corruption. And the outcome is for the righteous.
28:84: Whoever comes with a good deed, for him there is better than it, and whoever comes with an evil deed, those who do evil are punished only with what they did.
28:85: Indeed, the One Who made the Quran obligatory upon you will return you to a place of return. Say: 'My Rabb knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear misguidance.'
28:86: You were not hoping that the Book would be cast to you, but it is a mercy from your Rabb, so never be of those who back the disbelievers.
28:87: And let them not turn you away from the verses of Allah after they have been sent down to you, and call to your Rabb, and never be of the polytheists.
28:88: Do not invoke another deity along with Allah. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face. The judgment is His, and to Him you will be returned.
